labelingGuide: isDeal=true when the item reports a specific M&A transaction between named parties in which one acquires control of (>50% of, or all of) a company, or a material business/asset package, and the item is a DEAL EVENT: (a) signing/announcement of a definitive agreement; (b) a formal public offer, tender offer or takeover bid (including improved/extended offers); (c) an amendment/revision of agreed terms; (d) a shareholder approval, go-shop expiry or similar status step of that deal; (e) completion/closing. Completed deals count and share the dedupeGroup of their announcement. Asset purchases count only when the assets are a material business or asset package (e.g. oil & gas assets, a retail network); minority or non-controlling stakes, small property/equipment purchases and spectrum/licence-only grabs do not. SPAC business combinations and fund-to-fund mergers count as deals. isDeal=false for: rumors, talks, reports of exploration, non-binding or preliminary proposals; withdrawn, dropped or terminated deals; litigation, regulatory, political or labor commentary about a pending deal; merger-arbitrage and investment-analysis commentary; earnings releases (even if they mention a deal); law-firm investor alerts; and SEC 8-K hits that merely mention a merger agreement (e.g. credit facilities). For deals, acquirer/target are canonical company names as a human would write them (acquirer = the party paying/absorbing, target = the company or business acquired; for mergers the surviving/public parent is the acquirer). Names are taken from the headline where possible, otherwise from other outlets covering the same deal or from the SEC filing text. dedupeGroup is a slug shared by every item (Google News or SEC) that describes the same deal, including its amendments and completion; null for non-deals. For SEC items, title is synthesised as "<registrant> — <form> filing (<items>)" in the same way src/feeds.js does; the registrant may be either the acquirer or the target.
